projectSummary: Gives the proportional, territory-based account of pectoral innervation that the tertiary chapter states categorically: the medial nerve supplies the lower part of the muscle in most but not all people, and the lateral nerve supplies the proximal part. Because the abstract attributes the proportions to earlier work, the numbers are carried as reported-from, not as this source's own measurement.

study.intervention: Anatomical review of pectoral nerve course with reported proportions.
study.population: The article states that in 62 per cent of patients the medial pectoral nerve courses through the pectoralis minor muscle to innervate the lower half or two thirds of the pectoralis major, and that in the other 38 per cent it exits around the lateral aspect of the pectoralis minor.

title: The anatomy of the pectoral nerves and its significance to the general and plastic surgeon.
